findings.title: `source_bar_stamping` guard accepts a plain string
findings.description:
`TimeMeaning` is a `StrEnum` (timestamps.py:37). A str-mixin enum member hashes and compares as its string value, so the bare string `"period_start"` is a member of `SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS` and passes the membership check. The market then stores a plain `str`, not `TimeMeaning`. Any identity check downstream, such as `market.source_bar_stamping is TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START`, returns False for that market.

The sibling fields are guarded differently. `continuity_kind` uses `isinstance` and rejects `"adjusted"` (markets.py:102-104, test_markets.py:123). `session_mode` also rejects `"regular"`. Only this field uses membership. No test covers a string stamping, and canonical bytes are identical for the string and the enum, so equality and hashing will not expose the difference.

Fix: check `isinstance(self.source_bar_stamping, TimeMeaning)` before the membership check, and add a `"period_start"` case to `REJECTED_MARKETS`. I have not executed this. The conclusion rests on how StrEnum hashing and equality work.

findings.title: Constructor docstring promises "any iterable" but the types say `tuple`/`frozenset`
findings.description:
The `Market` docstring (lines 74-75) says `session_calendars` and `adjustment_bases` "accept any iterable". The annotations at lines 83 and 85 declare `tuple[SessionCalendarRef, ...]` and `frozenset[AdjustmentBasis]`. Under the strict pyright configuration the project requires, a caller passing a list gets a type error, so the docstring is wrong for static callers.

At runtime, a non-iterable such as `session_calendars=None` reaches `tuple(refs)` (markets.py:144) or `frozenset(bases)` (markets.py:161) and raises a bare `TypeError`. That falls outside the `CoreModelError` hierarchy that the module uses for invalid fields. The tests do not show the gap because `make_market` builds its kwargs as `dict[str, Any]` (test_markets.py:42 and the surrounding dict).

Fix: decide one contract. Either annotate the constructor inputs as `Iterable[...]` and store the normalized types, or keep the tuple/frozenset annotations and correct the docstring. In both cases, convert non-iterable input into `InvalidMarketError`.

findings.title: Duplicated validation helpers across `markets.py` and `instruments.py`
findings.description:
`_require_instance` in `instruments.py:80-86` is the same function as `markets.py:132-138`. The only difference is the exception class (`InvalidInstrumentError` versus `InvalidMarketError`). The `type is str` plus non-empty check in `Instrument.__post_init__` (instruments.py:69-75) also repeats `_require_nonempty_str` (markets.py:123-129). The project rule is "do not duplicate logic", and `instruments.py` already imports from `markets.py`.

Fix: move one helper into a shared module that takes the error class as a parameter, and use it from both files.

findings.title: The calendar-reference test cannot catch most embedding bugs
findings.description: `test_calendars_are_referenced_by_id_only` makes a no-op copy with `replace(EQUITY_FIXTURE)` and checks that one date literal is absent from the bytes. It would not catch an embedded calendar whose coverage bounds or sessions are encoded in another form, and it does not check that the calendar id is present. A stronger test would assert that the `calendar_id` string appears in the canonical bytes and that the `$date` and `covered_` keys do not.

findings.title: Market and instrument golden rows pin only the hash
findings.description:
The new comment says the market and instrument rows are "hash only", without a reason. The file's header allows `None` for "long values", and an existing row cites its measured size (line 267, "1632" bytes). The market rows give no size. These rows are the ones most likely to drift, and a mismatch cannot be diagnosed from bytes. I could not verify the hash values here.

Fix: pin the bytes for at least the market rows, or record the measured size in the comment.

findings.title: Fixture registries are checked against hand-copied lists
findings.description:
`FIXTURE_CALENDARS` and `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES` are built from hand-written tuples. `test_fixture_calendars_are_keyed_by_their_own_ids` (test_calendars.py:316-324) compares the mapping's values against the same four names written again, so a new calendar left out of the tuple passes the test. The instrument test hard-codes `len == 5` (test_instruments.py:208-211). The uniformity test would fail only if a market used the omitted calendar.

Fix: derive the registry from the module namespace, or add a test that scans the module for `Calendar` instances and checks each one is registered.

findings.title: The uniformity test does not exercise the per-market fields its docstring claims
findings.description: The module docstring says "one code path serves every market", but the test body (lines 50-63) reads only the calendar, the period end, and the multiplier. It never reads `source_bar_stamping`, `continuity_kind`, or `adjustment_bases`. The Kalshi market is `PERIOD_END` stamped, yet the test feeds it a `PERIOD_START` timestamp without reading the stamping. Nothing consumes those fields yet, so the test cannot show uniform handling of them. The docstring should say what is covered.

findings.title: Extended-session literals match their wall-clock comments
findings.description: I checked the nine extended sessions and the coverage bounds against UTC epoch arithmetic. 2026-10-26 00:00 UTC is 1792972800 seconds. The EDT-to-EST switch on Nov 2, the Nov 4 holiday gap, and the 17:00 early close on Nov 5 all match their comments. `test_calendars.py:310-313` checks that the extended and regular calendars share session dates.

findings.title: The import-boundary check for markets and instruments is live
findings.description: `_core_model_imports` returns package-relative names (`calendars`, `fixtures.markets`), so the `{"calendars", "canonical"}` set and the `startswith("fixtures")` test match real imports. The guard can fail. I confirmed this by reading `_core_model_imports` at lines 78-91.

structured_findings.summary: Constructor docstring promises "any iterable" but the types say `tuple`/`frozenset`
The calendar-reference test cannot catch most embedding bugs
Market and instrument golden rows pin only the hash
Fixture registries are checked against hand-copied lists
The uniformity test does not exercise the per-market fields its docstring claims
Extended-session literals match their wall-clock comments
The import-boundary check for markets and instruments is live
